input.passage: In the cloud forests of Ecuador, the glass frog Hyalinobatrachium valerioi exhibits an unusual form of parental care. The male, whose translucent belly reveals his beating heart and internal organs, guards clutches of eggs laid on the undersides of leaves hanging over streams for several ______ he defends them from predatory wasps and periodically moistens them with water from his own skin to prevent the developing embryos from drying out.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 긴 비필수 관계절과 전치사구 뒤에서 두 독립절의 경계를 찾고, 'during this time'이 어느 절에 속하는지 문맥으로 판단해야 하는 두 단계 구조로 만들었다.
input.explanation: 'The male ... guards clutches ... for several weeks'가 첫 번째 독립절이고, 'during this time, he defends ...'가 두 번째 독립절이므로 둘 사이에는 세미콜론이 와야 한다. 'during this time'은 앞서 말한 '몇 주'를 가리키므로 뒤 절의 첫머리에 놓이는 것이 자연스럽고, 도입 부사구라서 뒤에 쉼표를 찍는다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B와 D는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 세미콜론을 'during this time' 뒤에 두어 이 구가 앞 절에 붙는데, 'for several weeks during this time'은 의미가 중복되고 어색하며 뒤 절이 시간 표지를 잃는다.
input.explanation_en: The text contains two independent clauses. The first is "The male ... guards clutches ... for several weeks," and the second is "during this time, he defends them ...," so you need a semicolon between them. The phrase "during this time" points back to the "several weeks," so it belongs at the start of the second clause, and because it's an introductory phrase, a comma follows it. That makes A the answer. B and D connect the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts the semicolon after "during this time," which attaches the phrase to the first clause; "for several weeks during this time" is redundant and awkward, and the second clause loses its time marker.

input.passage: In her 2019 novel The Lamplighter's Daughter, Welsh author Carys Penhallow borrows the slow, ornate cadence of Victorian fiction to tell a distinctly modern story. Her narrator, a retired archivist who spends her evenings cataloging letters left behind by a nineteenth-century mill ______ the archivist gradually realizes that the letters' faded complaints about wages and fatigue echo her own memories of factory work decades later.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 긴 비필수 관계절 뒤에서 닫는 쉼표와 두 독립절 사이 경계(쉼표+등위접속사)를 동시에 판단해야 하도록 구성했다. 오답들은 각각 하나의 조건만 충족한다.
input.explanation: "who spends ... mill owner"는 주어 "Her narrator"와 동사 "never names" 사이에 끼어든 비필수 관계절이므로, 앞에 쉼표가 있으면 뒤에도 쉼표로 닫아야 합니다. 또한 "the archivist gradually realizes..."도 독립절이므로, 두 독립절은 쉼표와 등위접속사로 연결해야 합니다. B는 두 조건을 모두 충족합니다. A는 세미콜론으로 두 절을 바르게 나누지만, 관계절을 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 주어와 동사 사이에 쉼표가 들어간 것처럼 보이고 관계절이 제대로 닫히지 않습니다. C는 "and"를 넣었지만 관계절을 닫는 쉼표가 없고, D는 관계절은 닫았지만 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접합 오류가 됩니다.
input.explanation_en: The clause "who spends ... mill owner" is a nonessential relative clause that sits between the subject "Her narrator" and the verb "never names." Since it opens with a comma, it also has to close with one. On top of that, "the archivist gradually realizes..." is another independent clause, so the two independent clauses need a comma plus a coordinating conjunction between them. Choice B meets both requirements. Choice A separates the clauses correctly with a semicolon, but it leaves out the comma that closes the relative clause, so the interruption is never properly closed. Choice C adds "and" but also skips the closing comma, and Choice D closes the relative clause but joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice.

content.text:
Passage idea: a dash opens an interrupter, so the blank has to close it with a matching dash.

Passage: "The Atacama Desert's fog oases, known locally as lomas, depend almost entirely on moisture drawn from coastal clouds. The camanchaca—a dense marine fog that rolls inland from the Pacific on winter ______ condenses on the leaves of cacti and shrubs, sustaining plant communities in a region where measurable rain may not fall for years."

The subject is "The camanchaca," and its verb is "condenses." The interrupter begins with a dash, so it has to end with a dash: "mornings—condenses."

Options:
A) mornings, condenses (the marks don't match)
B) mornings; condenses (a semicolon here cuts the subject off from its verb)
C) mornings—condenses (correct)
D) mornings condenses (no punctuation, so the interrupter is never closed)

input.passage: The Atacama Desert's fog oases, known locally as lomas, depend almost entirely on moisture drawn from coastal clouds. The camanchaca—a dense marine fog that rolls inland from the Pacific Ocean on winter ______ condenses on the leaves of cacti and shrubs, sustaining plant communities in a region where measurable rain may not fall for years.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: The interrupter set off by a dash comes between the subject (camanchaca) and the verb (condenses), so the student has to spot the opening dash and also see that the subject-verb link cannot be cut. The comma option is the trap for students who skim.
input.explanation: 주어 The camanchaca와 동사 condenses 사이에 대시로 시작한 동격 삽입구가 있으므로, 삽입구를 닫을 때도 대시를 써야 합니다. 그래서 C가 정답입니다. A는 삽입구를 닫는 쉼표가 자연스러워 보이지만, 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫으면 부호가 짝을 이루지 않습니다. B의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 있어야 하는데, 앞부분에는 동사가 없고 주어와 동사가 끊어집니다. D는 삽입구를 닫지 않아 'winter mornings condenses'처럼 잘못 읽힙니다.
input.explanation_en: There is an interrupting appositive between the subject "The camanchaca" and its verb "condenses," and it opens with a dash, so it has to close with a dash too. That makes C correct. A may look natural, but closing a dash-opened interrupter with a comma leaves the marks unmatched. B uses a semicolon, which needs an independent clause on each side; here the part before it has no verb, and the semicolon cuts the subject off from its verb. D never closes the interrupter, so it misreads as "winter mornings condenses."

content.text:
Subject-verb agreement after a long modifier, plus tense from context.

Passage: "Behavioral economist ... studied ... In a 2019 field experiment, the set of default contribution rates offered to new employees at a regional credit union, which ranged from 3 to 8 percent of salary, ______ how much workers ultimately saved, even among employees who said they had carefully reviewed every option."
Subject "set" singular; past context. Options: A "were shaping" (plural), B "shaped" correct, C "have shaped" (plural, present perfect), D "shaping" (participle, no main verb). Need two partially valid: A past but plural; C plural agrees with "rates"; D... ok. Maybe make A "shape" (plural present) — anyway fine.

input.passage: In a 2019 field experiment led by behavioral economist Hiroshi Tanabe, the menu of default contribution rates presented to newly hired employees at a regional credit union, which ranged from 3 to 8 percent of salary, ______ how much the workers ultimately saved, even among employees who reported having carefully compared every available option.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 문장 주어(menu)와 동사 사이에 복수 명사(rates, employees)와 긴 관계절을 넣어 일치 판단을 흐리게 하고, 2019년 과거 문맥으로 시제까지 확인하게 하는 두 단계 판단을 요구했다. 정동사가 없는 분사형도 오답으로 넣었다.
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the menu'이고, 'of default contribution rates'와 'which ranged...' 관계절은 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 주어와 맞으면서 2019년 실험이라는 과거 문맥에도 맞는 정동사가 필요하므로 B 'strongly shaped'가 정답이다. A는 과거 시제이지만 복수 동사 'were'를 써서 가까이 있는 'rates'에 잘못 일치시켰다. C의 'have'도 복수형이라 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다. D는 분사일 뿐이어서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "the menu." The phrase "of default contribution rates" and the clause "which ranged..." just modify that subject. So you need a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject and also fits the past-tense context of a 2019 experiment, which makes B, "strongly shaped," the answer. A is in the past tense, but its verb "were" is plural, so it wrongly agrees with the nearby noun "rates." C's "have" is also plural, so it doesn't agree with the singular subject either. D is only a participle, so the sentence would be left without a main verb.

content.text:
Topic: modern social change history — e.g., 1880s Danish cooperative dairies? Let's design.

Passage: "In the 1880s, Danish farmers began pooling their milk at cooperative creameries, facilities owned jointly by the farmers who supplied them______ each member, regardless of herd size, received a single vote in decisions about how the creamery was run."

Blank after "supplied them": options: D "them; each" – correct? Wait can't repeat word before blank. Blank after "them" then options start with punctuation. Options: A ", each" (comma splice), B " each" (run-on), C ", and, each"? Better: C "—and each" hmm that's acceptable actually. Use C ": and each"? Make distractors: A comma; B no punctuation; C ", which" ... "which each member received a vote" ungrammatical. Hmm medium: partially plausible. Alternative C: "—each" with appositive dash? Dash there would be acceptable to separate clause. Avoid. Use C ", so" — comma + conjunction grammatical but logic wrong? That's style; avoid. Use C "and" with no comma — run-on-ish; SAT treats "and" without comma between independent clauses as error. OK.

Options: A ", each" B " each" C " and each" D "; each". Format as text options: ", each" etc.

input.passage: In the 1880s, Danish dairy farmers began pooling their milk at cooperative creameries, processing plants owned jointly by the very farmers who supplied them______ each member, regardless of how many cows he kept, received a single vote in decisions about how the creamery would be run. Historians credit this arrangement with spreading democratic habits through the Danish countryside.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격 수식어(processing plants owned jointly by ... supplied them)로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'each member ... received a single vote ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C는 등위접속사 and를 썼지만 두 독립절 사이에 필요한 쉼표가 없고, 긴 동격 수식어 때문에 문장 경계가 흐려진다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank is an independent clause that ends with a long appositive (processing plants owned jointly by ... supplied them). The text after the blank, "each member ... received a single vote ...," is also an independent clause, with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so D is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B runs the two clauses together with no punctuation, which creates a run-on sentence. C uses the conjunction "and" but leaves out the comma needed before it when it joins two independent clauses, and the long appositive makes the break between the clauses hard to see.
input.design: The long appositive before the blank hides where the first independent clause ends. Because of that, students need to find both clauses and then compare a comma, no punctuation, "and" with no comma, and a semicolon to choose the answer.

content.text:
Passage idea: an engineer and a structure. Something like: "In 2019, engineers at the Dutch firm ... built a pedestrian bridge from 3D-printed stainless steel ______ the 12-meter span..." Better to aim for a medium boundary question: a long modifier, then the clause boundary.

Draft: "The Falkirk Wheel, a rotating boat lift that opened in Scotland in 2002 to reconnect two canals, needs remarkably little power to operate ______ because the water-filled gondolas on either end always weigh the same, the motors only have to overcome friction."

Correct: "operate:" (colon introducing an explanation). Wrong options: "operate," (comma splice), "operate, and" (no; actually ", and because..." is a valid coordinate clause, so it's wrong for a different reason), "operate" with no punctuation (run-on). Since ", and" could be defended, I'll use a semicolon followed by an extra word instead: "operate; because" + clause. That's grammatical too. So the options will be: A) colon, B) comma, C) no punctuation, D) "operate, because"? But "because ... , the motors..." after a comma is still a comma splice. Fine.

input.passage: The Falkirk Wheel, a rotating boat lift that opened in Scotland in 2002 to reconnect two canals separated by a 24-meter drop, needs remarkably little power to operate______ because the water-filled gondolas at either end of its arms always weigh the same, its electric motors have to overcome only friction as the wheel turns.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 긴 동격구 뒤의 주절 "The Falkirk Wheel ... needs remarkably little power to operate"는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "because ..., its electric motors have to overcome ..."도 종속절이 앞에 붙은 독립절이다. 뒤 절이 앞 절의 내용을 설명하므로, 독립절 두 개를 잇고 설명을 이끄는 콜론을 쓴 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이다. C는 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D의 ", and"는 형식상 가능해 보이지만, 'because' 절은 둘째 절의 이유를 나타내는 것이지 첫째 절과 대등하게 나열되는 정보가 아니므로 설명 관계를 제대로 드러내지 못한다. 그러므로 가장 적절한 표기는 A이다.
input.explanation_en: Once you skip past the long appositive, the main clause "The Falkirk Wheel ... needs remarkably little power to operate" is an independent clause. What follows the blank, "because ..., its electric motors have to overcome only friction," is also an independent clause that just opens with a dependent clause. The second clause explains the first, so A's colon is correct: it joins two independent clauses and introduces an explanation. B is a comma splice, because it joins two independent clauses with only a comma. C is a run-on, because it joins them with no punctuation at all. D can look acceptable, but "and" treats the two clauses as equal, parallel facts, which hides the fact that the second clause explains why the first one is true.
input.design: A long appositive hides where the main clause ends, and the clause after the blank begins with an introductory "because" phrase, so it can look like a dependent clause. Students have to find both independent clauses and then see that the second one explains the first.

input.passage: Trained as a textile designer in Lagos before turning to sculpture, Nigerian artist Ngozi Adebayo builds towering figures from discarded fishing nets she collects along the Gulf of Guinea coast. The knotted, sun-bleached strands of nylon that give each piece its distinctive texture ______ visitors of both the craft traditions Adebayo learned as a student and the environmental damage that abandoned gear causes in coastal waters.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 주어 strands와 빈칸 사이에 of nylon, that절 수식어를 넣어 단수 명사(nylon, texture, piece)에 끌려 단수 동사를 고르게 유도했다. 동시에 비정동사(분사)를 배제하는 두 번째 판단이 필요하다.
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'strands'(복수)이고, 'of nylon'과 'that give each piece its distinctive texture'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어이다. 따라서 복수 정동사 A 'remind'가 맞다. B 'reminds'와 D 'has reminded'는 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'texture'나 'nylon'에 맞춘 단수 형태여서 복수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C 'reminding'은 분사라서 정동사가 될 수 없고, 그러면 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "strands." The phrase "of nylon" and the clause "that give each piece its distinctive texture" both just modify it. So the sentence needs a plural main verb, and A, "remind," is correct. B ("reminds") and D ("has reminded") are singular forms that match nearby nouns like "texture" or "nylon" instead of the actual subject. C ("reminding") is a participle, which can't work as a main verb, so choosing it would leave the sentence without one.

content.text:
Medium form/structure item on art and architecture criticism. Test: subject-verb agreement after a long modifier, combined with tense/finite verb choice.

Passage idea: "The series of cantilevered balconies that architect Lina Ferreira designed for the hillside library in Porto, each angled to catch a different hour of afternoon light, ______ critics who had dismissed her earlier work as merely decorative."
The subject is "series" (singular), and the main verb is required. Options:
A) have won over: plural, wrong
B) winning over: not a finite verb
C) were winning over: plural
D) has won over: correct

The distractors are partly plausible because "balconies" is plural and sits close to the blank. Option B could look acceptable to a reader who takes the sentence as a fragment. Context check: the singular head noun "series".

input.passage: The series of cantilevered balconies that architect Lina Ferreira designed for a hillside library in Porto, each one angled to catch a different hour of afternoon light, ______ many critics who had once dismissed her work as merely decorative.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'series'이며, 'of cantilevered balconies'부터 'afternoon light'까지는 모두 수식어구이므로 빈칸에는 단수 정동사가 필요하다. D는 단수 정동사이므로 정답이다. A와 C는 정동사라는 점은 맞지만, 빈칸 가까이에 있는 복수 명사 'balconies'나 'light' 앞의 수식어에 이끌린 복수형이어서 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. B는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "series." Everything from "of cantilevered balconies" through "afternoon light" only modifies that subject, so the blank needs a singular finite verb. D supplies one, so it is correct. A and C are finite verbs, but they are plural forms that seem to agree with the nearby plural noun "balconies." Because of that, they don't agree with the singular subject. B is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb and make it a fragment.
input.design: To answer correctly, students have to see past a long modifier and the plural "balconies" sitting close to the blank, find the singular head noun, and then also confirm that the blank needs a finite verb. A and C each pass one of these checks, and B is a fragment.

content.text:
Design: subject-verb agreement after long modifier, with tense context.

Passage: Among the Pirahã... avoid real controversial? Choose: whistled languages. "The whistled form of Spanish used on La Gomera, one of the Canary Islands, allows herders to communicate across deep ravines. Silbo Gomero, as linguists call it, replaces the vowels and consonants of spoken Spanish with changes in pitch and duration. A recent study of listeners who learned the system as children ______ that such speakers process whistled sentences in the same brain regions that handle ordinary speech."
Subject "A recent study" singular; past context "recent study" → "found". Options: A) have found (plural, perfect), B) finding (nonfinite), C) found, D) were finding (plural). Hmm, C vs "finds" — keep only one singular. Good.

input.passage: On La Gomera, one of the Canary Islands, herders have long communicated across deep ravines using Silbo Gomero, a whistled form of Spanish that replaces spoken vowels and consonants with shifts in pitch and duration. A 2005 study of islanders who had learned the whistled system as children ______ that these listeners process whistled sentences in the same brain regions that handle ordinary spoken language.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 빈칸이 주어 'A 2005 study'와 긴 전치사구·관계절(복수 명사 islanders, children) 뒤의 정동사 자리라 가까운 복수 명사에 끌리면 틀리며, 정동사 필요 여부와 단수 일치를 둘 다 판단해야 한다.
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'study'이고, 'of islanders who had learned the whistled system as children'은 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 맞는 정동사가 필요하며, 2005년이라는 과거 시점과도 맞는 C의 'found'가 정답이다. A와 D는 정동사이지만 복수형이라서 가까이 있는 복수 명사 'islanders'나 'children'에 맞춘 오답이다. B의 'finding'은 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "study." The phrase "of islanders who had learned the whistled system as children" only modifies it. That means the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and C, "found," works and also fits the past time frame set by "2005." A and D are finite verbs, but they're plural forms that agree with the nearby plural nouns "islanders" or "children," not with the actual subject. B, "finding," is a participle, so it would leave the sentence without a main verb.

content.text:
Subject-verb agreement after a long modifier, set in astronomy. Topic: the light curve of a magnetar, or the rings of Chariklo.

Passage: "The rings encircling Chariklo, a small icy body orbiting the Sun between Saturn and Uranus, ______ astronomers in 2013, when the object passed in front of a distant star and the starlight dimmed briefly twice on each side."
The subject is "rings," so the verb has to be plural. Since it's 2013, the past tense is needed: "surprised." The trouble is that in past tense singular and plural look the same. Better to use the present: "The rings ... continue to puzzle astronomers." Options:
A) continues to puzzle
B) continue to puzzle
C) continuing to puzzle
D) has continued to puzzle
That gives two singular distractors and one participle, which works.

input.passage: First detected in 2013, when the object passed in front of a distant star and the starlight dimmed briefly on either side of it, the two narrow rings encircling Chariklo, a small icy body that orbits the Sun between Saturn and Uranus, ______ astronomers, who had assumed that such a tiny world lacked the gravity to hold ring material in place.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'the two narrow rings'(복수)이고, 빈칸에는 본동사가 와야 한다. 따라서 복수 정동사인 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 정동사이지만 단수형이다. 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'Chariklo'나 'a small icy body'를 주어로 착각하면 고르게 된다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없어져 문장이 불완전해진다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "the two narrow rings," which is plural, and the blank must supply the main verb. That makes B, a plural finite verb, correct. A and D are finite verbs, but they are singular. You might pick them if you mistake the nearby singular nouns "Chariklo" or "a small icy body" for the subject. C is a participle, so it would leave the sentence without a main verb, making it incomplete.
input.design: 긴 도입 분사구와 동격 수식어가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어서, 주어를 찾는 판단과 정동사인지 확인하는 판단을 두 단계로 해야 한다.
